# aws-identity

IAM least privilege (wildcard grants, session duration) and Cognito pool posture (MFA, deletion protection) as measured by the iam-role/cognito dump readers.

## Detected anti-patterns

### `AF-IAM-001` — Inline role policy grants wildcard actions (high)

`"Action": "*"` in an Allow statement grants every present and future action in the matched service scope — least privilege is broken by construction, and the policy document in the dump proves it directly.

Remediation: Enumerate the actions the role actually calls (start from CloudTrail `LookupEvents` on the role's sessions) and replace the wildcard with the observed set.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html#grant-least-privilege

### `AF-IAM-002` — Inline role policy grants wildcard resources (high)

`"Resource": "*"` applies the grant to every resource the action accepts — including resources created after the policy was written.

Remediation: Scope `Resource` to the ARNs the workload touches; where the ARN set is genuinely dynamic, use condition keys to bound it.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html#grant-least-privilege

### `AF-IAM-003` — Role session duration exceeds 12 hours (low)

`MaxSessionDuration` above 43200 stretches the window a leaked session credential stays valid; the dump declares the number.

Remediation: Keep `MaxSessionDuration` at the 1-hour default unless a measured workload requires longer, and record the requirement.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use.html

### `AF-IAM-004` — Cognito user pool has MFA off (medium)

`MfaConfiguration: OFF` removes the second factor for every user in the pool — a declared posture, not an inference.

Remediation: Set `OPTIONAL` or `ON` per the pool's risk profile; if OFF is deliberate (machine-only pool), record the exception.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/user-pool-settings-mfa.html

### `AF-IAM-005` — Cognito user pool has deletion protection inactive (low)

`DeletionProtection` not ACTIVE leaves the pool deletable by any caller with `cognito-idp:DeleteUserPool` — one API call destroys the identity store.

Remediation: Activate deletion protection on pools that hold real identities; recreating a pool does not recreate the users.

Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/user-pool-settings-deletion-protection.html
